ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: clothes warm enough for {SUBJECT}
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: The coming season will be colder than this colonist's clothes let them bear. They want something to wear that keeps them comfortable through it: not a coat for the stores, but clothes warm enough for them, worn.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: What {FOR_nameDef} wears keeps {FOR_objective} comfortable down to {TARGET}°C, the season's usual cold. Something like {THING} would do it, or anything as warm {FOR_pronoun} may wear. Promised, {FOR_pronoun} goes and puts on the warmest thing in store that would do.

plain.li: These clothes were fine in summer. They won't be fine for {SUBJECT}.
I've worked out what I'll need for {SUBJECT}, and it isn't what I'm wearing. Something like {THING} would do it.
My clothes were made for somewhere warmer than this. I need clothes made for here.
[fall,morning] The mornings have teeth already. I'd like to be dressed for {SUBJECT} before it bites properly.
[winter,evening] My fingers went white out there today, and it took ages to feel them again.
[snow] I came back from the fields with snow down my collar and up my sleeves.
[old] The cold gets into my bones these days. Something warm for {SUBJECT}, before I'm stiff all through.
[tribal] Skins sewn double, fur on the inside. That's what my people wore through the dark months.
[medieval] A good wool cloak and something thick under it. That's all I'm asking for {SUBJECT}.
[child] My coat's too thin. My hands go red and then they stop hurting, and I think that's bad.

warm.li: Nothing fancy. Something warm enough that I'm not shivering by midday. I'll mend it myself when it tears.
I don't need a pile of coats in the stores. I'd just like to be warm in what I'm wearing.

blunt.li: My clothes won't get me through {SUBJECT}. Make me some that will.
I'm cold already, and it's going to get worse. Fix it.

cheerful.li: Something warm and fluffy, maybe with a hood! I don't mind if I look like a haystack.
I've picked out the warmest thing I can think of. It's {THING}. Please?

gloomy.li: [cold] I lose the feeling in my hands every time I go out. One day it won't come back.
I've been cold since the leaves fell, and the worst of it hasn't even started.

cold.li: Cold slows the hands and dulls the mind. Dress me for {SUBJECT} and you'll get a full day's work out of me.
What I wear is fit for milder weather than we'll have. That's a problem with a simple answer.

plain.li: Warm all the way through, for once.
Let it snow. I'm dressed for it now.

warm.li: Thank you. Whoever stitched this, I owe them a favour.

blunt.li: Now the cold can go and bother someone else.

cheerful.li: I look like a walking haystack and I've never been happier!

gloomy.li: I can feel my fingers again. Mixed blessing. They hurt.

plain.li: More shirts, then, one on top of the other.

blunt.li: If I lose a toe, I'm leaving it on the council's table.

cold.li: Expect less from me until spring.

plain.li: It's getting colder, and I'm still dressed for the weather we had.
Still nothing warm enough to wear, and {SUBJECT} isn't waiting.

gloomy.li: I've stopped feeling my ears. That's probably fine.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: clothes cool enough for {SUBJECT}
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: On hot land, the coming season will be hotter than this colonist's clothes let them bear. They want something to wear that keeps them comfortable in it: a wide hat, a duster, something light, whatever the colony has or can make.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: What {FOR_nameDef} wears keeps {FOR_objective} comfortable up to {TARGET}°C, the season's usual heat. Something like {THING} would do it. Promised, {FOR_pronoun} goes and puts on the best thing in store that would do.

plain.li: I'm dressed for somewhere milder. These clothes will cook me in {SUBJECT}.
Something with a brim, something light. I can't spend {SUBJECT} squinting and sweating.
[summer] By noon my shirt's soaked through and stuck to my back. There must be something better to wear.
[hot] The sun's like a hand pressing down on my head. A hat, a duster, anything that keeps it off.
[lowtech] Where I'm from, people wore loose cloth against the sun, head to foot. I'd like the same here.
[old] Heat like this is hard on me. Something cooler to wear would help more than you'd think.
[day] Midday, and I'm wearing the wrong clothes for it again.

warm.li: Nothing fancy. Just something that lets the air through.
Something for my head, mostly. The rest of me can cope.

blunt.li: These clothes are too hot for this place. Find me some that aren't.

cheerful.li: A big floppy hat! Please. I've always wanted to be a big floppy hat person.

gloomy.li: I'll be lying in the shade like a dog by midsummer, in these.

cold.li: Heat costs work hours. The right clothes give them back.

plain.li: Shade on my head and air on my arms. Much better.

cheerful.li: Look at the brim on this!

cold.li: I can work through noon now.

plain.li: I'll keep to the shade, then.

blunt.li: Don't ask why I'm slow at noon.

gloomy.li: A long hot season in the wrong clothes.

plain.li: Still sweating through the same clothes.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a sauna for the cold months
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: On cold land, someone chilled to the bone, getting on in years or fond of company wants a small, hot room to warm up in. With Dubs Bad Hygiene, a sauna heater and its room; without it, a sauna of the colony's own: a small closed room with a seat and a heater kept hot (a fire, before electricity).

plain.li: A sauna. Hot stones, steam, and nothing to do but sweat out the cold. That's my wish.
My bones are frozen through. An evening in a sauna would thaw them.
One small room, kept hot, with somewhere to sit. That's all a sauna is, and it would change the winter.
[snow] It's snowing again. Picture coming in from that to a hot sauna.
[old] My joints ache all winter. Heat is the only thing that helps.
[lowtech] Hot stones and a ladle of water. People have done it since before anyone wrote things down.
[lowtech] A little hut with a fire, sealed up tight, and a bench to sweat on. My people built one wherever they wintered.
[evening] I'd like to end a cold day somewhere hot, just once, before bed.

warm.li: We could all sit in there together, talking and sweating. It brings people close.
Somewhere warm to go when the cold wears everyone down. It would do us all good.

blunt.li: A hot room and a bench. It's not much to ask in a place like this.

cheerful.li: Steam, heat, and a roll in the snow afterwards! I'll go first.
Imagine it: sweating like a pig in midwinter. I can't wait.

gloomy.li: It's going to be a long, cold winter. A sauna would make it bearable.
The cold has been in me since autumn. Nothing gets it out.

cold.li: Heat eases sore muscles and lifts spirits in a cold climate.
A small heated room costs little to run and keeps people working through the winter.

plain.li: I sat in the heat until my head swam. Best evening this winter.
I went in frozen and came out pink. Thank you.

warm.li: Come and sit. There's room for everyone.

blunt.li: Good. Close the door, you're letting the heat out.

cheerful.li: I ran out into the snow afterwards and shouted, then ran straight back in.

gloomy.li: Warm at last. I'll be cold again tomorrow, but I know where to go now.

plain.li: I'll stay frozen, then.
Still dreaming of a sauna.
Another cold day, and nowhere hot to sit at the end of it.
